decisions.reason: The NFT-detail cover sizing and cropping rule does not change referral counters, badges, or referral-code metadata.
The source changes NFT-detail cover presentation and does not alter badge definitions, milestones, storage, or effects.
Changing the NFT-detail cover display does not affect which book, referral code, badges, or prize tickets transfer with NFT ownership.
The source explicitly concerns the cover shown after selecting an NFT from the dashboard, not the separately scoped landing-page cover, whose rules remain unchanged.
The NFT-detail cover issue does not change landing-page hero copy, layout, emphasis, or mobile behavior.
The source does not request any change to FAQ text or informational content.
The same message separately establishes that failed mints must not appear as owned NFTs, but the source cover-display modification does not change that dashboard ownership rule.

The client's uncertainty about viewing the book is an observed issue potentially caused by a failed mint, not a decision changing holder-only access, encryption, ownership verification, or the gated-viewer flow.
NFT-detail cover presentation does not alter the PDF asset, IPFS storage, Pinata provider, or takedown capability.
The source reports an ETH mint and NFT-detail display issue and does not change the deferred fiat-buyer wallet or reward-access behavior.
The NFT-detail cover sizing rule does not affect the landing-page counter for sales remaining until the next prize draw.

The same message separately raises an unresolved first-mint no-referral edge case, already represented by an AMBIGUOUS Event, but the cover-display modification does not change the random-reward allocation state.
